analysis:
Changed behavior: EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift (head L448-458) now passes the process environment into makeSegmentedPagedBackend. EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift adds `import Foundation`, an `environment` parameter, and two operator env switches. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION (default on unless "0") sets PagedKVPoolConfig.retainedFreeSegmentBytes to min(2 GiB, grant/8). DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS (default on when retention is on) sets hostZeroedSegments. The BackendPreparation hunk is plumbing only. The GLM path is untouched and never reaches this factory.

Security-relevant observation, relating to T-028 (residual KV data in GPU memory), TB-007 and A-001: free KV segments are now kept across requests instead of being retired on release. The patch comment says retention avoids the per-segment device zero fill and fence. Prompt-derived KV from a prior consumer's request can therefore sit in retained, reusable segments longer. A consumer's data could reach another request only if the pool or kernels read page regions that were not rewritten or masked, or if reuse skips zero-fill or re-initialisation. The PagedKVPool and PagedKVBackend implementations (retainedFreeSegmentBytes and hostZeroedSegments semantics, scrubbing on reuse or teardown, accounting against GlobalKVCacheBudget) are not in the supplied evidence. I cannot confirm or rule out a cross-request or cross-tenant exposure, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.

T-028 text should be re-checked to say that retained free segments hold stale plaintext KV until overwritten, and whether that data is zeroed on idle unload or shutdown. The memory bound of at most grant/8 (2 GiB cap) appears to stay inside the admitted grant, but I could not verify its interaction with budget accounting. The env switches are operator-controlled. The operator is already ADV-001 with memory access (T-014), so they add no new privilege. Neither switch touches the SSD prefix cache (T-041), attestation, or the coordinator protocol.

Next pass should inspect PagedKVPool (segment retention, host zero-fill, reuse initialisation, release and teardown paths) and the tests.
